summary: p95 latency regression in eu-west after enabling FP8 kernel (hosted) — rollback executed
description:
Customer (NordicBank) reported a latency regression in eu-west beginning ~30–45 minutes after FP8 kernels were enabled for a subset of hosted traffic.

Issue summary
- Symptom: increased p95 end-to-end latency, most visible on chat completions; customer also reported increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) on streaming.
- Correlation: aligned with regional rollout flag enabling FP8 attention kernel path.
- Impact: customer observed p95 latency increase of ~18–30% (varies by route/model), intermittent timeouts on longer prompts (rare).

Customer report (from Support intake)
- Time window: 2026-02-23 10:50–12:10 UTC (first noticed), persisted until rollback.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (streaming=true).
- Example request IDs (customer-provided): euw-req-7f2c9e1a, euw-req-80c41b7d, euw-req-91db7c20.

Initial impact assessment (Redwood)
- Region: eu-west only.
- Suspected cohort: FP8 enabled canary cohort (model+region gate).
- Metrics: TTFT p95 elevated; tokens/sec roughly flat to slightly improved; error rate unchanged.

Environment
- Runtime: 1.22.0-rc* cohort in eu-west canary pools.
- GPU: mixed H100/A100 pools (hosted).

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Route traffic to eu-west canary cohort (kernel_mode=fp8) using internal header override.
2) Run Top Hosted Models benchmark suite v3 case: chat, tool-calling disabled, prompt length bucket ~2k–6k tokens, max_output_tokens 256.
3) Observe TTFT p95 and scheduler queue depth increase vs baseline kernel_mode=bf16.

Dashboards / data (internal)
- Grafana: "FP8/INT8 Rollout - Canary" (eu-west) — panels: TTFT p50/p95 by kernel_mode, queue_depth_p95, prefill_latency_ms_p95, decode_tpot_ms_p95.
- Query tags: model, gpu_sku, kernel_mode, region, route.
- Notable: spike is concentrated in prefill (TTFT) and coincides with increased launch overhead on attention kernel path for certain shape regimes.

Working hypothesis
FP8 attention kernel path introduces higher per-request overhead in prefill for certain prompt-length/head-dim regimes, and the scheduler prefill/decode mix in eu-west amplified it (higher concurrency / queue depth) leading to p95 regression despite comparable raw throughput.

resolution:
Resolved by rolling back FP8 kernel enablement (attention path) in eu-west for affected hosted models/cohorts. Metrics returned to baseline within ~10 minutes. Root cause suspected to be increased prefill overhead for a specific shape regime under FP8 attention, amplified by scheduler mix/concurrency in eu-west. Guardrail added via hotfix to disable FP8 for the problematic shape bucket and fall back to baseline kernels; FP8 remains behind flags and will be re-enabled only after perf-canary stability and customer-specific validation.

Customer-facing outcome
- Immediate rollback completed; latency returned to expected range.
- Redwood will coordinate any re-enable with a controlled cohort and explicit opt-out for NordicBank if requested.

Follow-ups
- Add prompt_length_bucket dimension to canary alerting for TTFT p95.
- Validate eu-west driver/CUDA/container pinning consistency before next rollout.
- Link this regression to perf sprint decision log/ADR guardrails during next review.
